# Phylogenetic Terminology

- **Taxonomy**:  the study of naming and classifying things
- **Taxon**: A taxonomic unit (e.g., a species, genus, family, order, class)
- **Sister Taxa**: each other's closest relatives
- **Systematics**: the study of the evolutionary relationships of organisms
- **Phylogeny**: a hypothetical reconstruction of relationships
- [Monophyletic] **Clade**: A group of taxa that are each others' closest relatives / share a common ancestor more recently than they do with any other taxa
- **Apomorphy**: A trait that defines a clade

# Avian Apomorphies: Feathers 

- All birds (and some non-avian dinosaurs) have feathers
- Feathers are dead structures and are constantly replaced (through *molt*)
- Filamentous, soft, flexible, lightweight
- Diverse structure and function

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/feathers.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([Cornell Lab of Ornithology](https://academy.allaboutbirds.org/feathers-article/))

# Avian Apomorphies: Beak

- All birds have beaks (= bills)
- Diverse in form and function, but always toothless and covered in a horny sheath
- No other bills / beaks in animal kingdom (though the platypus bill comes close)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.6\linewidth]{images/toco.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([*Ramphastos toco*](https://macaulaylibrary.org/asset/71099091))

# Avian Apomorphies: Gizzard

- Posterior portion of stomach
- Bird "chewing" organ
- Thickness, muscluature, and quantity of grit / stones determined by diet. 

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/gizzard.jpg}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny ([*Wikipedia*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proventriculus))

# Avian Apomorphies: External Eggs

- Most complex reproductive cells of any animal
- Protected and provisioned with food
- Only vertebrate clade where no species have live young 

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/eggs.jpg}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*New York State Museum*](https://nysm.nysed.gov/research-collections/biology/ornithology/collections/bird-egg-collection)

# Avian Apomorphies*: Syrinx

- Vocal organ at the base of trachea 
- C.f. mammalian *larynx*: no folds
- Sounds from vibrating membranes and cartilage 
- Can be used to mimic speech (parrots, crows, and mynas)  
\* absent in New World Vultures

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/syrinx.jpg}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*Hornbill syrinxes, Wikipedia*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrinx_(bird_anatomy))

# Avian Apomorphies*: Lightweight Bones

- Lightwight, strong, bones
- Mostly hollow (air-filled spaces = "pneumatized")  
\* divers like loons in particular have denser bones  


\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/bone.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*National Audubon Society Bird Guide Training Curriculum*](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301801651_Bird_Guide_Training_Curriculum_Advanced_Level)


# Skeletal Structures: Uncinate Processes 

- Horizontal, backwards bone projections from ribs
- Reinforce rib cage and provide attachment point for muscles

\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*Wikipedia*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncinate_processes_of_ribs)

# Skeletal Structures: Furcula  

- a.k.a. Wishbone
- Compresses and rebounds like a spring in flight

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.4\linewidth]{images/furcula.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*Wikipedia*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furcula) 

# Skeletal Structures: Wings

- Modified forelimbs
- Carpometacarpus / metacarpus is a set of fused hand bones that support the primary flight feathers

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.8\linewidth]{images/wing.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*Wikipedia*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_wing)

# Skeletal Structures: Specialized Legs

- Birds are mostly digigrade (toe-walkers)
- Fused leg bones: tibiotarsus (below femur) and tarsometatarsus; equal length in long-legged birds for balance
- Opposable rear toe called hallux unique in vertebrates

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.39\linewidth]{images/leg.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*Wikipedia*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_wing)

# Skeletal Structures: Perching Mechanism

- Tendons lock toes around perch

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.7\linewidth]{images/perching.png}
\end{figure}  
\hfill \tiny [*Encyclopedia Brittanica*]

# Adaptation

- An adaptation is a phenotypic trait that increases fitness (survival and reproduction) in a specific environment
- Adaptation is also a process of evolutionary change in a population that results in increased fitness

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/adaptive.jpg}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny [Cornell Lab of Ornithology](https://www.allaboutbirds.org/news/why-evolution-goes-wild-on-islands-the-science-of-adaptive-radiation/)


# Birds can be considered an adaptive radiation

- Adaptive Radiation: An evolutionary process where an ancestral species rapidly diversifies into multiple new species specializing on diverse resources; also refers to the taxa resulting from this process

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/adaptive.jpg}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny [Cornell Lab of Ornithology](https://www.allaboutbirds.org/news/why-evolution-goes-wild-on-islands-the-science-of-adaptive-radiation/)
